item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In Deutschland gibt es erstmals einen Parlamentspräsidenten aus den Reihen der in Teilen als rechtsextrem eingestuften AfD. Der Landtag in Sachsen-Anhalt wählte in seiner konstituierenden Sitzung am Dienstag den AfD-Abgeordneten Tobias Rausch zu seinem Präsidenten. Weil er bei der geheimen Wahl 48 der 82 abgegebenen Stimmen bekam, löste dies eine parteipolitische Debatte auch auf Bundesebene aus. Denn die AfD und das sie unterstützende BSW verfügen zusammen nur über 44 Stimmen. Die SPD forderte von der CDU Aufklärung, ob deren Abgeordnete für Rausch gestimmt hatten. Dies werde auch Thema im Koalitionsausschuss der schwarz-roten Regierung am Mittwoch in Berlin werden, kündigte SPD-Fraktionschef Matthias Miersch an. CDU/CSU-Fraktionschef Thorsten Frei sagte, er sehe die Wahl in Magdeburg "mit allergrößter Besorgnis". Das gelte auch dafür, dass Rausch vier Stimmen mehr als erwartet bekommen habe. Zugleich wies er es als "reine Spekulation" zurück, dass CDU-Abgeordnete für diese vier Stimmen verantwortlich seien. Aber die Wahl an sich sei "in höchstem Maße bedenklich und besorgniserregend". Am Nachmittag wurde zudem der AfD-Politiker Hans-Thomas Tillschneider zu einem der Landtags-Vizepräsidenten gewählt. Bei 82 abgegebenen Stimmen erhielt er 44 Ja-Stimmen. Es gab 38 Nein-Stimmen und keine Enthaltungen. Rausch hatte 48-Ja-Stimmen bekommen, bei 29 Nein-Stimmen und 5 Enthaltungen. AfD-Wahlsieger Ulrich Siegmund hat angekündigt, sich im Dezember im Landtag als Kandidat für das Amt des Ministerpräsidenten zur Wahl stellen zu wollen. Ihm fehlt eine Mehrheit, weil die anderen Parteien keine Koalition mit der AfD eingehen wollen. Auch das BSW lehnt eine formelle Zusammenarbeit mit der AfD ab, hat aber angekündigt, sich in einem dritten Wahlgang enthalten zu wollen. Dann würde für die Wahl Siegmunds eine einfache Mehrheit ausreichen - dann müsste der AfD-Politiker aber mit einer Minderheitsregierung regieren, was er bisher abgelehnt hat. Bis zu einer erfolgreichen Wahl eines neuen Regierungschefs ist Ministerpräsident Sven Schulze (CDU) geschäftsführend weiter im Amt. CSU-Landesgruppenchef Hoffmann warf der AfD vor, "demokratiefeindlich" zu sein. Das sehe man daran, dass die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt nur 100 Prozent AfD und keinen Kompromiss eingehen wolle. Es gehe der AfD nur darum, das demokratische System zu zersetzen. Er glaube, dass die AfD durch das Verhalten Siegmunds "ein Stück weit entzaubert" werde, auch für ihre Wähler. Denn offensichtlich wolle sie die Zusage nicht einhalten, etwas zu ändern.

item.title: London stocks gain on softer oil, easing gilt yields; Defence shares fall
item.description: The UK's FTSE 100 advanced on Tuesday as a retreat in bond yields and softer oil prices calmed investors following last week's bond-market volatility, while losses in defence stocks capped gains.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The UK's FTSE 100 advanced on Tuesday as a retreat in bond yields and softer oil prices calmed investors following last week's bond-market volatility, while losses in defence stocks capped gains. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose 0.4% to 24,215.33 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) also climbed 0.4%. Brent crude oil declined 2% as resilient Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns, although continued security risks in the Middle East limited further losses. Government borrowing costs also eased after 10- and 30-year gilt yields , surged to multi-decade highs last week, as investors weighed persistent inflation and debt concerns. Bank of England policymaker Catherine Mann [USN:L8N45S0KH TEXT:"warned"] that inflation has become embedded in the UK economy and could become further entrenched as wage negotiations pick up early next year Markets see about a 90% probability of a 25-basis-point or larger BoE rate hike in November, according to LSEG data. Defence stocks fell, with BAE Systems (BAES.L) , Babcock International (BAB.L) and Rolls-Royce (RR.L) down between 2% and 4%. A Times report said the government was considering delaying plans to set out a path towards [USN:L8N45S0CO TEXT:"lifting defence spending to 3% of GDP"]. Informa (INF.L) was among top FTSE 100 gainers, rising 3%. The exhibitions group said it would [USN:L4N45S0CT TEXT:"buy events organiser Clarion"] for £2.24 billion ($2.98 billion) and spin off its Taylor & Francis academic publishing division "While separating off the academic publishing business means there is little else to support the business if live events struggle, it at least recognises where the real growth in the business will continue to be," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG. On the FTSE 250, shipping services provider Clarkson (CKN.L) rose 2.2% after forecasting annual underlying [USN:L6N45S0BI TEXT:"pretax profit above market expectations"]. ASOS (ASOS.L) dropped 9.6% after [USN:L6N45S0OD TEXT:"media reports"] said customers of the online fashion retailer had received push notifications saying it had been hacked and threatening to leak information. The firm said basic personal information might have been accessed but that it did not believe payment-card information or account passwords had been affected. ($1 = 0.7528 pounds)

item.title: Emera bulks up for power demand boom with $10 billion Canadian Utilities deal
item.description: Emera said on Tuesday it would buy peer Canadian Utilities for C$14.3 billion ($10.02 billion) in stock, strengthening its financial muscle as power companies ramp up investments to tap into booming demand.
item.dc:creator: Katha Kalia
item.content:encoded: Emera (EMA.TO) said on Tuesday it would buy peer Canadian Utilities (CU.TO) for C$14.3 billion ($10.02 billion) in stock, strengthening its financial muscle as power companies ramp up investments to tap into booming demand. The deal, which will create one of Canada's top power providers with an enterprise value of about C$72 billion, comes when utilities across North America move ahead with costly upgrades of aging grid and transmission infrastructure. "As demand rises from electrification trends and major infrastructure development, the combined company will be better positioned to help meet growing energy needs," Emera CEO Scott Balfour, who will lead the combined company, said in a statement. US power firms NextEra Energy (NEE.N) and Dominion Energy (D.N) in May [USN:L4N41V0YN TEXT:"agreed to merge"] in a $66.8 billion deal amid soaring electricity demand fueled by the rapid expansion of data centers supporting the adoption of AI. Emera said the deal would support a planned C$32 billion capital program through 2030, with an expected annual rate-base growth of 7% to 8%. The combined company will have about 6 million customers and a presence in high-growth markets through a portfolio of 12 regulated utilities. "Florida and Alberta will become the company's two largest jurisdictions, representing approximately 45% and 34% respectively," Balfour said in a conference call. DEAL CLOSING IN 2027 Under the offer, Class A shareholders of Canadian Utilities, excluding ATCO (ACOx.TO) , will receive 0.755 Emera shares and Class B shareholders will get 0.819 for each share held. The deal values Canadian Utilities' Class A shares at about C$51.57 each, a premium of roughly 0.7% to the stock's close on Monday, according to LSEG data. Meanwhile, ATCO, which holds nearly 37% of the outstanding non-voting shares and all outstanding voting shares of Canadian Utilities, will separate into a publicly traded industrial services company. Emera shares were down 1.2%, Canadian Utilities rose 1.4% and ATCO jumped 12.8% in morning trading. The deal is expected to close in the third or fourth quarter of 2027 and add to earnings per share in the first full year following the completion. The new company will operate as Emera and maintain its public company headquarters in Halifax. ($1 = 1.4270 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Becton Dickinson pledges $19 billion US investment in deal with government
item.description: Becton Dickinson became the first major US medical device company to strike a deal with the government to expand its domestic manufacturing, pledging $19 billion over several years in return for shelter from future tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Siddhi Mahatole
item.content:encoded: Becton Dickinson (BDX.N) became the first major US medical device company to strike a deal with the government to expand its domestic manufacturing, pledging $19 billion over several years in return for shelter from future tariffs. Under the agreement, the company on Tuesday said it plans to make capital, operational and supply chain investments in the US, with $3 billion earmarked for strategic manufacturing sites across the country. Shares of the medical device maker were up 2.4% in morning trading. The deal follows the Trump administration's [USN:L4N3TZ1L7 TEXT:"push"] to use tariff threats to spur domestic healthcare manufacturing, with [USN:L4N4470VR TEXT:"major drugmakers already pledging billions"] for new and expanded US production and research facilities. The agreement ties BD's US manufacturing commitments to relief from future tariffs on covered products and inputs under Section 232, subject to the final scope of the measures and the company meeting agreed milestones. "We think tariff clarity or the potential for levies to be 'less bad' than feared could be a clearing event for MedTech," said Jefferies analyst Mathew Taylor, adding "we wonder if there are more MedTech announcements in the works." The company plans to expand US production by about 5 billion essential medical consumables annually, raising the share it supplies domestically to roughly 80%. It also plans to manufacture all needles used in the US domestically using American-made steel. Becton Dickinson said it was not currently quantifying the financial impact of the agreement because the final tariff rates, product scope and timing have not yet been determined. The announcement builds on President Donald Trump's [USN:L1N45S036 TEXT:"statement on Monday"] that the company had agreed to invest $3 billion to bring manufacturing of essential medical products to the United States, with more than $1 billion going to Nebraska. In January, Becton announced a $110 million investment in Columbus, Nebraska, to expand prefillable syringe and cannula production, adding about 120 jobs, with syringe production expected to begin supplying customers in mid-2026.

item.title: Google enters massive 3.6-GW power deal with Constellation Energy
item.description: Google has contracted for 3,590 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy in the largest US power grid, with new nuclear energy accounting for about a quarter of that supply, the companies said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Laila Kearney
item.content:encoded: Google (GOOGL.O) has contracted for 3,590 megawatts of power from Constellation Energy (CEG.O) in the largest US power grid, with new nuclear energy accounting for about a quarter of that supply, the companies said on Tuesday. Constellation will make more than $4.3 billion of new investments in its fleet as part of the agreement, which involves adding capacity at several of the power company's nuclear reactors in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic regions, the companies said. Major tech companies are racing to secure massive amounts of electricity supplies to power data centers across the US by striking unprecedented power deals and reviving the country's nuclear industry. Over the last two years, Constellation unveiled an agreement to restart its [USN:L1N3LU103 TEXT:"Three Mile Island reactor "]in Pennsylvania to serve Microsoft (MSFT.O) data centers, while Google contracted [USN:L4N3W81GR TEXT:"to restart "]NextEra Energy's (NEE.N) nuclear power plant in Iowa. In the latest arrangement, Google entered into a 20-year power purchase agreement for 890 megawatts of electricity from multiple Constellation-owned nuclear power plants, which would be upgraded to produce more electricity from existing reactors. Electricity from the first of the upgraded plants is expected to be delivered in 2028, the companies said. Google also entered into a 15-year supply agreement for an additional 2,700 megawatts of power from Constellation in the PJM power grid. That power is not tied to a specific generation source and serves as long-term revenue certainty for Constellation's operating plants, Google said. Shares of Constellation were up by more than 13% on Tuesday to $304.04 by mid-morning. Maryland-based Constellation is the largest US nuclear power plant operator and owns a major fleet of natural-gas-fired power plants as well as geothermal energy following its [USN:L4N3O60SW TEXT:"acquisition of electricity producer"] Calpine Corp earlier this year. "We’re committed to meeting our growth responsibly by actively investing in clean, reliable power that brings new capacity to our nation's grids," said Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of energy and power, in a statement. The 11 nuclear units expected to be upgraded as part of the arrangement with Google are in Illinois, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey, within the footprint of the largest US electric grid -- PJM Interconnection. Rising electricity demand driven largely by the data center expansion has contributed to a more than 11-fold increase in PJM capacity prices since 2024 and left the grid with a power shortfall. In response, PJM management has proposed requiring data center customers connected to the 13-state grid to either bring their own power or face being shut off from grid power remotely in times of peak demand. The deal between Google and Constellation is in response to PJM's "bring your own power" proposal. It also creates a "practical model for how major power consumers can expand new supply alongside growing operational requirements, without state or federal mandates," the companies said. Google and Constellation also agreed on a strategic framework that can be replicated to develop power generation, battery storage, and a flexible power use model known as "demand response" in other parts of the US, the companies said. Joe Dominguez, chairman, president and CEO of Constellation, said the arrangement with Google is a "model for how technology companies and the energy industry can work together to responsibly develop the digital economy and invest in our nation’s energy infrastructure in a way that delivers grid-wide benefits for all, funded by private entities."

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq hit record highs as Treasury yields stall, oil slips
item.description: The benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record highs on Tuesday as Treasury yields eased from multi-year highs and oil prices fell, while investors looked ahead to the upcoming quarterly earnings season.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: The benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record highs on Tuesday as Treasury yields eased from multi-year highs and oil prices fell, while investors looked ahead to the upcoming quarterly earnings season. Most of the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks ticked higher, with Meta (META.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) , Amazon.com (AMZN.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) all up between 0.5% and 1.7%. Chip designer Nvidia (NVDA.O) climbed 1.1%, pushing the market valuation of the world's most valuable company close to the $6 trillion mark. Optimism surrounding the AI trade and hopes of strong corporate earnings lifted US equities lately, further boosting the bull market that began in October 2022 despite higher energy prices and a volatile summer for bond markets that fueled concerns about tighter monetary policy. "The economy continues to be more resilient than many expected, and corporate earnings remain strong, but the big change is rising interest rates," said David Miller, chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds. "Investors are now dealing with meaningfully higher long-term rates ... I am still bullish on equities, but the hurdle has gone up significantly." Government bond yields eased across the curve, including a 5.3-basis-point decline for the benchmark 10-year bond . A soft payrolls report last week reduced chances of an interest rate hike in October, with traders now seeing a near 79% chance of a hold, though a December rate hike remains largely priced in, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. On Tuesday, at least four Fed officials, including New York Fed President John Williams, are slated to deliver public remarks. All 11 S&P 500 sectors were trading higher, with utilities (.SPLRCU) and real estate (.SPLRCR) leading the gains. At 11:33 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 359.08 points, or 0.70%, to 51,626.98, the S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 66.16 points, or 0.86%, to 7,840.66 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) gained 228.58 points, or 0.83%, to 27,705.89. Oil prices, meanwhile, fell around 2% as resilient Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns. The third-quarter earnings season will kick off next week. Analysts on average expect S&P 500 earnings to jump over 30% year over year in the quarter, thanks largely to AI-related stocks, according to LSEG data. Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) climbed 6.5% after the [USN:L6N45S0Y5 TEXT:"chip designer"] raised its 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, citing strong demand for its chips used in data centers. Chipmaker AMD (AMD.O) gained 3.6% after CEO Lisa Su said [USN:L6N45S09C TEXT:"the company planned"] to substantially increase chip supply in 2027 to meet booming AI demand. Constellation Energy (CEG.O) was the top gainer on the S&P 500, up 13.9% after Alphabet's Google (GOOGL.O) entered into a 3,590-megawatt power [USN:L6N45S04O TEXT:"deal"] with the company. Option Care Health (OPCH.O) jumped 32.7% after drug distributor McKesson (MCK.N) and private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice [USN:L4N45S0SZ TEXT:"agreed to buy"] the infusion therapy provider in a deal worth about $5.8 billion, including debt. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 2.93-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 21 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 48 new highs and 123 new lows.

item.title: Catalan separatist Puigdemont set to return home after court lifts arrest warrant
item.description: Spain's two top courts cleared the way on Tuesday for self-exiled Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont to return without being arrested, just as Spain is gearing up for an early national election.
item.dc:creator: Joan Faus, Emma Pinedo
item.content:encoded: Spain's two top courts cleared the way on Tuesday for self-exiled Catalan separatist leader Carles Puigdemont to return without being arrested, just as Spain is gearing up for an [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"early national election"]. The Constitutional Court ruled that an amnesty law for Catalan separatists applies to embezzlement charges against Puigdemont. Shortly afterwards, the Supreme Court responded by lifting a warrant for Puigdemont's arrest. The likely homecoming of the former Catalan head of government could further unsettle an already volatile political landscape ahead of the November 29 election. Puigdemont fled to Belgium in 2017 after holding an independence referendum for his region that Madrid had declared illegal. "It's a great victory for President Puigdemont and the two other exiled" leaders in Belgium, Jordi Turull, secretary general of Puigdemont's party Junts, told reporters. "They held firm, they resisted, they prevailed in Europe and today they have prevailed against the Spanish state." He declined to say when Puigdemont might return, but ruled out his running in the upcoming election. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez had enacted the amnesty under a 2023 agreement between his Socialist Party and two Catalan parties, including Puigdemont's Junts, in exchange for their support for him to remain prime minister. The move triggered intense social and political opposition from the government's critics at the time. The Supreme Court had initially ruled that the amnesty did not apply to the crime of embezzlement, which meant Puigdemont and others could still be arrested on charges of embezzling the funds that were spent on the referendum. But the Constitutional Court, which has a progressive-leaning majority, ruled in an appeal that disallowing the amnesty for embezzlement unconnected with private enrichment would violate the purpose of the amnesty law. "The ruling is in line with expectations, as we had always maintained that the amnesty law was constitutional and also consistent with European Union law," Puigdemont's lawyer, Gonzalo Boye, told Reuters. A year ago, Junts withdrew its support for the minority central government. Unable to pass laws, Sanchez [USN:L8N45R0N4 TEXT:"called"] the snap election on Monday. Sanchez told reporters on Tuesday he did not regret launching the amnesty, and welcomed the court ruling. "I believe the important message is that of coexistence among Catalans," he said. FRESH DRAMA Although separatism has [USN:L8N4590Z7 TEXT:"lost ground"] and Junts is trailing in opinion polls, Puigdemont's return could spark fresh political drama. Spain's conservative People's Party is leading in opinion polls ahead of the election and may need to seek the support of Junts and other centre-right parties to govern. Catalonia unilaterally [USN:KBN1CB272 TEXT:"declared independence"] from Spain in 2017 after the referendum. Although some 90% of voters backed independence, Catalans who wanted to remain part of Spain mostly boycotted the ballot and many polling stations were shut. Puigdemont then fled the country, while several of his former ministers, including Turull, stayed and were jailed until later being pardoned by Sanchez.

item.title: Canada's TSX edges up as bond yields retreat, utility shares advance
item.description: Canada's benchmark stock index inched higher on Tuesday, with utilities leading gains, as a pullback in global bond yields and easing oil prices supported sentiment, although weakness in energy and mining shares capped advances.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P
item.content:encoded: Canada's benchmark stock index inched higher on Tuesday, with utilities leading gains, as a pullback in global bond yields and easing oil prices supported sentiment, although weakness in energy and mining shares capped advances. The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) rose 0.19% to 35,587.45 points by 10:08 a.m. ET and was on track for its third straight day of gains. Utilities (.GSPTTUT) rose 1%, leading gains, as global bond yields retreated Emera (EMA.TO) said it would acquire Canadian Utilities (CU.TO) in an [USN:L4N45S0P5 TEXT:"all-stock deal worth C$14.3 billion"] ($10.02 billion), creating one of Canada's largest utilities Emera fell 2%, while Canadian Utilities inched higher marginally. ATCO (ACOx.TO) jumped 12.8% after saying it would spin off into a standalone publicly traded industrial services company called New ATCO Oil fell by more than $2 as rising Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns, with Brent Crude dipping below $100 a barrel The energy sector (.SPTTEN) fell 1.4%, while the materials sector (.GSPTTMT) dropped 0.7%, limiting broader market gains The yield on the US benchmark 10-year Treasury note dipped after hitting a 24-year high on Monday, while the yield on the Canadian 10-year government bond also edged lower, offering some respite to markets "I'd be focused more on interest rates, the 10-year yield in the United States, than I would be on energy prices, although they're related," said Matt Skipp, president at SW8 Asset Management "A moderating oil price seems to have the potential to lower yields, as investors worry less about inflation," Skipp added Concerns over persistent inflation and rising government debt, however, continue to keep bond and equity markets on edge Markets are pricing in at least one more quarter-point rate hike from the US Federal Reserve and a 25-basis-point increase from the Bank of Canada before year-end, according to LSEG compiled data

item.title: Californians blast Trump remark that Iran could 'take out' Los Angeles, San Diego
item.description: President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could "take out" a major US city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could "take out" a major US city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California's Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. Trump, speaking at a [USN:L1N45R0ZC TEXT:"political rally"] in the state's farm belt on Monday, discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to "see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did." "And again, remember, with the war, it's just artificial, it's a little bit high, it's a small price to pay," he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertilizer and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war. "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let 'em take out Los Angeles, let 'em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it's going to be over with very soon," he said. "It's essentially almost over with," Trump went on. "But it's going to end very soon, and it's going to end one way or the other." On Tuesday, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark. "The media freakout over President Trump’s comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating U.S. cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung said in a social media post. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money." Trump has shrugged off cost-of-living concerns stemming from the Iran conflict before, and he previously downplayed his concerns about the potential for Iran or its allies to launch an attack on US soil. EARLY VOTING UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA The comment in rural Nebraska, a state Trump won with more than 55% of the vote in the 2024 presidential election, targeted Democratic-run cities in California, a solidly Democratic state the president often criticizes. Monday's comments prompted a backlash from California officials. California Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, denounced the Republican president as "deranged and dangerous." "After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should 'take out' Los Angeles and San Diego," he wrote on X. Newsom, who has positioned himself as a major political foil to Trump and is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, juxtaposed a video clip of Trump in Nebraska with mention of the president's previous rhetoric to justify deploying US military troops to Los Angeles and other cities to fight crime and enforce immigration. California's early voting for the November midterm elections started on Monday. The president's Republican Party has hoped to win more races in the state in recent years, including this year's gubernatorial election. Newsom championed the redrawing of California's [USN:S0N3WN09U TEXT:"congressional map"] last year to favor Democrats in this year's election after Trump pushed for conservative-led Texas to [USN:L1N3TX13Y TEXT:"redraw its map"] to boost Republicans. One of the Republicans running in a competitive race in a redrawn California district near San Diego, Jim Desmond, distanced himself from Trump's remarks. "I vehemently disagree with President Trump’s comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander in Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland," he wrote on X. "No American city is expendable, and no American family should ever be treated as collateral damage." Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, a Democrat and former member of Congress, likewise chided Trump for his comments. "The president of the United States suggested that a foreign government attack Los Angeles. His statements against our city are dangerous and could potentially compromise our safety," Bass said in a statement. Los Angeles and San Diego rank as the largest and second-largest cities in California by population. More than 115,000 activity-duty service members are also stationed in San Diego, including Naval Base San Diego, the largest on the United States' west coast. "My constituents — including many active duty service members, veterans, and their families — are not acceptable collateral damage in Trump’s stupid war," US Representative Sara Jacobs, a Democrat, said in a social media post.
